cohort: 195 women from the Dunedin arm of the ProLong study, who had delivered vaginally, were assessed 20 years after their index birth.
finding: Most Levator ani muscle (LAM) avulsions and external anal sphincter (EAS) defects appear to be caused by the first vaginal birth, with subsequent vaginal deliveries not significantly increasing the risk of further trauma.
mod_finding: Subsequent vaginal deliveries after the first were found to be unlikely to cause further Levator ani muscle (LAM) trauma or external anal sphincter (EAS) defects.
